description: Deterministic message generation and checksum oracle shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. Every variant (socket baseline, shared-memory copy, shared-memory slot view, batched, process restart/recovery) must reproduce the same checksum over the same message sequence.
payloadFormula: payload(messageIndex, size)[j] = (messageIndex + j) & 0xFF, for j in [0, size)
checksumFormula: checksum(messageIndex, payload, length) = fold: h = messageIndex*31, then h = h*31 + payload[i] for i in [0, length), all as wrapping 64-bit arithmetic

ringProtocol.note: capacity/protocolVersion at offsets 0/4; writerSeq at offset 64 (own cache line); readerSeq at offset 128 (own cache line); slots begin at offset 192. Single-writer/single-consumer SPSC cursor protocol identical in structure to the spsc-ring-buffer lab, applied to a memory-mapped shared segment instead of process-heap memory.

recoveryScenario.note: The producer publishes an initial batch, the harness kills the consumer process, then starts a fresh consumer process that resumes reading from the segment's own recorded readerSeq (not from message index 0) and a fresh producer that resumes writerSeq via resumeWriter(). Correctness requires the resumed consumer to see every message exactly once, with none re-delivered or skipped.
